arxiv-2011-13419.title: THIS IS A DRAFT VERSION AND IS SUBJECT TO REVISION. Distributed Optimisation With Communication Delays The authors are with Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, Kanpur (India) 208016 (Email: shuubham@iitk.ac.in, ketan@iitk.ac.in).
arxiv-2011-13419.creator: Shuubham Ojha, Ketan Rajawat
arxiv-2011-13419.description: Abstract This paper discusses distributed optimization over a directed graph. We begin with some well known algorithms which achieve consensus among agents including Fast Row-stochastic-Optimization with uncoordinated STep-sizes (FROST) [ 1 ] , which possesses linear convergence to the optimum. However FROST works only over fixed topology of underlying network.

arxiv-2102-02755.title: Instance-based learning using the Half-Space Proximal Graph Under review in Pattern Recognition Letters
arxiv-2102-02755.creator: Ariana Talamantes, Edgar Chavez
arxiv-2102-02755.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ariana Talamantes, Edgar Chavez. The primary example of instance-based learning is the k k -nearest neighbor rule (kNN), praised for its simplicity and the capacity to adapt to new unseen data and toss away old data. The main disadvantages often mentioned are the classification complexity, which is O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) , and the estimation of the parameter k k , the number of nearest neighbors to be used.

arxiv-2103-04055.title: Visualizing Robot Intent for Object Handovers with Augmented Reality
arxiv-2103-04055.creator: Rhys Newbury, Akansel Cosgun, Tysha Crowley-Davis, Wesley P. Chan, Tom Drummond, Elizabeth A. Croft
arxiv-2103-04055.description: Abstract Humans are highly skilled in communicating their intent for when and where a handover would occur. However, even the state-of-the-art robotic implementations for handovers typically lack of such communication skills. This study investigates visualization of the robot’s internal state and intent for Human-to-Robot Handovers using Augmented Reality.

arxiv-2103-05247.title: Pretrained Transformers As Universal Computation Engines
arxiv-2103-05247.creator: Kevin Lu, Aditya Grover
arxiv-2103-05247.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kevin Lu, Aditya Grover. We investigate the capability of a transformer pretrained on natural language to generalize to other modalities with minimal finetuning -- in particular, without finetuning of the self-attention and feedforward layers of the residual blocks. We consider such a model, which we call a Frozen Pretrained Transformer (FPT), and study finetuning it on a variety of sequence classification tasks spanning numerical computation, vision, and protein fold prediction.

arxiv-2109-09270.title: Magnetic Fields in Massive Star-Forming Regions (MagMaR) II. Tomography Through Dust and Molecular Line Polarization in NGC 6334I(N)
arxiv-2109-09270.creator: Paulo C. Cortés, Patricio Sanhueza, Martin Houde, Sergio Martín, Charles L. H. Hull, Josep M. Girart, Qizhou Zhang, Manuel Fernandez-Lopez, Luis A. Zapata, Ian W. Stephens, Hua-bai Li, Benjamin Wu, Fernando Olguin, Xing Lu, Andres E. Guzmán, Fumitaka Nakamura
arxiv-2109-09270.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Paulo C. Cortés, Patricio Sanhueza, Martin Houde, Sergio Martín, Charles L. H. Hull, Josep M. Girart, Qizhou Zhang, Manuel Fernandez-Lopez, Luis A. Zapata, Ian W. Stephens, Hua-bai Li, Benjamin Wu, Fernando Olguin, Xing Lu, Andres E. Guzmán, Fumitaka Nakamura. Here, we report ALMA detections of polarized emission from dust, CS( J = 5 → 4 J=5\rightarrow 4 ), and C 33 S( J = 5 → 4 J=5\rightarrow 4 ) toward the high-mass star-forming region NGC6334I(N).

arxiv-2111-12088.title: Cosmology and neutrino mass with the Minimum Spanning Tree 2020 Cosmology and neutrino mass with the Minimum Spanning Tree – 3
arxiv-2111-12088.creator: Krishna Naidoo, Elena Massara, Ofer Lahav
arxiv-2111-12088.description: Abstract The information content of the minimum spanning tree (MST), used to capture higher-order statistics and information from the cosmic web, is compared to that of the power spectrum for a ν ​ Λ \nu\Lambda CDM model. The measurements are made in redshift space using haloes from the Quijote simulation of mass ≥ 3.

arxiv-2209-14015.title: Funnel-based Reachability Control of Unknown Nonlinear Systems using Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2209-14015.creator: Sandeep Gorantla, Jeel Chatrola, Jay Bhagiya, Adnane Saoud, Pushpak Jagtap
arxiv-2209-14015.description: Abstract This paper aims to synthesize a reachability controller for an unknown dynamical system. We first learn the unknown system using Gaussian processes and the (probabilistic) guarantee on the learned model. Then we use the funnel-based controller synthesis approach using this approximated dynamical system to design the controller for a reachability specification.

arxiv-2212-03473.title: Bayesian multilevel multivariate logistic regression for superiority decision-making under observable treatment heterogeneity
arxiv-2212-03473.creator: X.M. Kavelaars, J. Mulder, M.C. Kaptein
arxiv-2212-03473.description: Abstract Background: In medical, social, and behavioral research we often encounter datasets with a multilevel structure and multiple correlated dependent variables. These data are frequently collected from a study population that distinguishes several subpopulations with different (i.e., heterogeneous) effects of an intervention.

arxiv-2305-05401.title: Learn to Sing by Listening: Building Controllable Virtual Singer by Unsupervised Learning from Voice Recordings
arxiv-2305-05401.creator: Wei Xue, Yiwen Wang, Qifeng Liu, Yike Guo
arxiv-2305-05401.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wei Xue, Yiwen Wang, Qifeng Liu, Yike Guo. The virtual world is being established in which digital humans are created indistinguishable from real humans. Producing their audio-related capabilities is crucial since voice conveys extensive personal characteristics. We aim to create a controllable audio-form virtual singer; however, supervised modeling and controlling all different factors of the singing voice, such as timbre, tempo, pitch, and lyrics, is extremely difficult since accurately labeling all such information needs enormous labor work.

arxiv-2307-13453.title: Monte-Carlo Tree Search for Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Preliminary Results
arxiv-2307-13453.creator: Yelisey Pitanov, Alexey Skrynnik, Anton Andreychuk, Konstantin Yakovlev, Aleksandr Panov
arxiv-2307-13453.description: Abstract In this work we study a well-known and challenging problem of Multi-agent Pathfinding, when a set of agents is confined to a graph, each agent is assigned a unique start and goal vertices and the task is to find a set of collision-free paths (one for each agent) such that each agent reaches its respective goal.

arxiv-2402-12755.title: Observation of Berry curvature in non-Hermitian system from far-field radiation
arxiv-2402-12755.creator: Xuefan Yin 1,2†, Ye Chen 2†, Xiaoyu Zhang 2, Zixuan Zhang 2, Susumu Noda 1, Chao Peng 2,3∗
arxiv-2402-12755.description: Abstract Berry curvature that describes local geometrical properties of energy bands can elucidate many fascinating phenomena in solid-state, photonic, and phononic systems, given its connection to global topological invariants such as the Chern number. Despite its significance, the observation of Berry curvature poses a substantial challenging since wavefunctions are deeply embedded within the system.

arxiv-2405-04513.title: Switchable Decision: Dynamic Neural Generation Networks
arxiv-2405-04513.creator: Shujian Zhang, Korawat Tanwisuth, Chengyue Gong, Pengcheng He, Mingyuan Zhou
arxiv-2405-04513.description: Abstract Auto-regressive generation models achieve competitive performance across many different NLP tasks such as summarization, question answering, and classifications. However, they are also known for being slow in inference, which makes them challenging to deploy in real-time applications. We propose a switchable decision to accelerate inference by dynamically assigning computation resources for each data instance.

arxiv-2412-08243.title: Hierarchical Context Alignment with Disentangled Geometric and Temporal Modeling for Semantic Occupancy Prediction
arxiv-2412-08243.creator: Bohan Li, Jiajun Deng , Yasheng Sun, Xiaofeng Wang, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng
arxiv-2412-08243.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bohan Li, Jiajun Deng , Yasheng Sun, Xiaofeng Wang, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng. Camera-based 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction (SOP) is crucial for understanding complex 3D scenes from limited 2D image observations. Existing SOP methods typically aggregate contextual features to assist the occupancy representation learning, alleviating issues like occlusion or ambiguity.

arxiv-2506-16512.title: Galactic echoes 2025 Galactic echoes – B
arxiv-2506-16512.creator: Rimpei Chiba, Jupiter Ding, Chris Hamilton, Matthew W. Kunz, Scott Tremaine
arxiv-2506-16512.description: Abstract Gaia has revealed a variety of substructures in the phase space of stars in the Solar neighborhood, including the vertical ‘Snail’ in ( z , v z ) (z,v_{z}) space. Such substructures are often interpreted as the incompletely phase-mixed response of the disc stars to a single perturbation, such as an impulsive encounter with a satellite galaxy.

arxiv-2509-17255.title: Agentic AI for Multi-Stage Physics Experiments at a Large-Scale User Facility Particle Accelerator
arxiv-2509-17255.creator: Thorsten Hellert, Drew Bertwistle, Simon C. Leemann, Antonin Sulc, Marco Venturini
arxiv-2509-17255.description: Abstract We present the first language-model–driven agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system to autonomously execute multi-stage physics experiments on a production synchrotron light source. Implemented at the Advanced Light Source particle accelerator, the system translates natural language user prompts into structured execution plans that combine archive data retrieval, control-system channel resolution, automated script generation, controlled machine interaction, and analysis.

arxiv-2606-18856.title: Approximate Structured Diffusion for Sequence Labelling
arxiv-2606-18856.creator: Nicolas Floquet, Joseph Le Roux, Nadi Tomeh

doe-osti-3013839-mechanical-solutions-sc.title: Mechanical Solutions Scan Report
doe-osti-3013839-mechanical-solutions-sc.creator: Avery, Becca, Milloway, Ria, Tacke, Jonathan M. et al.
doe-osti-3013839-mechanical-solutions-sc.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Power lines, poles, and towers are the backbone of the United States (U.S.) electric-power grid. These transmission and distribution networks route electricity from generator to loads. The characteristics of these routes are rapidly changing -- trending towards decentralized rene

pmc-10480066.title: Leaf functional diversity and environmental filtering in a tropical dry forest: Comparison between two geological substrates
pmc-10480066.creator: Valentina Sandoval‐Granillo, Jorge A Meave
pmc-10480066.description: The role of geological substrate in shaping plant community functional diversity remains poorly understood. Considering the involvement of leaves in the energy, water, and nutrient economics of plants, we hypothesized that leaves experience geology‐related filtering, which in turn shapes their functional attributes and community leaf functional diversity on different substrates.

pmc-10736259.title: EFFECTS OF CONSERVATIVE VALUES AND AGING KNOWLEDGE ON YOUNG ADULTS’ AGEISM AGAINST OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10736259.creator: Joseph Muraira, Erin Hulsman, Christian López, Derek Killingsworth, Kellee Bishop, Jenna Lao, Allyson Coldiron, Michael Barnett
pmc-10736259.description: Ageism – the stereotypes, prejudice, and discrimination of individuals solely based on age – is an unfortunately prevalent phenomenon for older adults to experience from young adults, and increased ageism among young adults has been associated with more conservative values and beliefs.

pmc-11350845.title: The Genetic Identification of Numerous Apicomplexan Sarcocystis Species in Intestines of Common Buzzard (Buteo buteo)
pmc-11350845.creator: Tautvilė Šukytė, Evelina Juozaitytė-Ngugu, Saulius Švažas, Dalius Butkauskas, Petras Prakas, Maciej Skoracki
pmc-11350845.description: Simple SummarySarcocystis parasites (Apicomplexa: Sarcocystidae) exhibit a complex life cycle necessitating two hosts and infect a wide range of mammals, birds, and reptiles. Birds of prey, positioned at the apex of the food chain, serve as definitive hosts for various Sarcocystis species.

pmc-11353228.title: The Mitogenome of the Subarctic Octocoral Alcyonium digitatum Reveals a Putative tRNAPro Gene Nested within MutS
pmc-11353228.creator: Alisa Heuchel, Åse Emblem, Tor Erik Jørgensen, Truls Moum, Steinar Daae Johansen
pmc-11353228.description: We sequenced and analyzed the complete mitogenome of a Norwegian isolate of the octocoral Alcyonium digitatum using the Ion Torrent sequencing technology. The 18,790 bp circular mitochondrial genome was found to harbor the same set of 17 genes, which encode 14 protein subunits, two structural ribosomal RNAs and one tRNA, as reported in other octocorals.

pmc-11632859.title: Enhancing efficacy of the MEK inhibitor trametinib with paclitaxel in KRAS-mutated colorectal cancer
pmc-11632859.creator: Susmita Ghosh, Fan Fan, Reid Powell, Yong Sung Park, Clifford Stephan, E Scott Kopetz, Lee M Ellis, Rajat Bhattacharya
pmc-11632859.description: Background:KRAS is frequently mutated in the tumors of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) and thus represents a valid target for therapy. However, the strategies of targeting KRAS directly and targeting the downstream effector mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK) via monotherapies have shown limited efficacy.

pmc-11680065.title: Characterization of the CBM50 Gene Family in Tilletia horrida and Identification of the Putative Effector Gene ThCBM50_1
pmc-11680065.creator: Ting Xiang, Deze Xu, Linxiu Pan, Dongyu Zhai, Yu Zhang, Aiping Zheng, Desuo Yin, Aijun Wang
pmc-11680065.description: Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are essential virulence factors in phytopathogens, particularly the extensively studied members from the CBM50 gene family, which are known as lysin motif (LysM) effectors and which play crucial roles in plant–pathogen interactions. However, the function of CBM50 in Tilletia horrida has yet to be fully studied. In this study, we identified seven CBM50 genes from the T.

pmc-12508632.title: Hydrogel Microspheres as Versatile Platforms for Biomedical Research: Design, Properties, and Applications
pmc-12508632.creator: Meng Yang, Yuanyuan Shi, Feng Wang, Xin Zhang, Jiayi Shao, Fan Yang, Hao Sun, Chong Zhang, Zheng Zhou, Jianyong Huang, Pengyu Lv, Patrick Shu‐Hang Yung, Jin Cheng, Hong‐Jie Huang, Jian‐Quan Wang
pmc-12508632.description: Hydrogel microspheres (HMs) are versatile biomaterials with biocompatibility and controlled release properties, widely applied in drug delivery, cell carriers, and tissue engineering. Their tunable material compositions (natural, synthetic, or composite polymers) and diverse fabrication techniques (e.g., microfluidics, electrohydrodynamic spraying) allow precise regulation of size, morphology, and functionality, supporting applications from musculoskeletal repair to dermatological therapy.

pmc-12564506.title: Valorization of Quince By-Products Using Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents (NADES): Extraction and In Vitro Digestion of Phenolic Compounds
pmc-12564506.creator: Erturk Bekar
pmc-12564506.description: Quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) processing generates peel and core by-product fractions that are underexploited resources with untapped potential for valorization in sustainable food systems. In this study, ultrasound-assisted extraction was performed using several choline chloride-based natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES, six formulations with distinct hydrogen-bond donors) and compared with 70% (v/v) ethanol.

pmc-12635145.title: Bridging the short-term and long-term dynamics of economic structural change
pmc-12635145.creator: James McNerney, Yang Li, Andres Gomez-Lievano, Frank Neffke
pmc-12635145.description: Economic development hinges on structural change, that is, transformations in what an economy produces. The field of economic complexity has investigated this process through two related but distinct branches: one studying how economies diversify, the other how the complexity of an economy is reflected in its output.

pmc-13286779.title: Preoperative exercise tolerance, nutritional-inflammatory markers, and outcomes after TEVAR for type B aortic pathology
pmc-13286779.creator: Haiyan Huang, Zhibing Ming, Wei Gu, Yuhong Tan, Jie Dai
pmc-13286779.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is the cornerstone treatment for type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but delayed discharge and mid-term major adverse events (MAEs) remain important clinical challenges. This single-center retrospective cohort study aimed to explore the associations of preoperative exercise tolerance, nutritional and inflammatory markers with short-term and mid-term outcomes in patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic pathology.MethodsA retrospective cohort study enrolled 300 consecutive patients who underwent TEVAR for type B aortic pathology (type B acute

pmc-13312254.title: Rare Leukemic Phase of Follicular Lymphoma With a High-Risk Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index (FLIPI) Score Treated With Bendamustine-Rituximab
pmc-13312254.creator: Niyati Bansal, Steve Thomas, Sri Gayathri Shanmugam
pmc-13312254.description: Follicular lymphoma is a slow-growing B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, accounting for approximately 20 to 30% of global cases. The leukemic phase is a rare presentation. It is often associated with high-risk characteristics, high tumor burden, slow progression, diagnostic challenges, and unfavorable prognosis.

pmc-13327904.title: Collagen nanofiber reinforced alginate hydrogel tube microbioreactors for cell culture
pmc-13327904.creator: Xinran Wu, Yakun Yang, Ying Pan, Yong Wang, Xiaojun Lian, Cheng Dong, Shue Wang, Aijun Wang, Wuqiang Zhu, Wansheng Liu, Yuguo Lei

pmc-13594953.title: Exploring the effect of tandem non-native non-F-type lectin carbohydrate-binding domains on Streptosporangium roseum α-L-Fucosidase activity
pmc-13594953.creator: Shivangi, Madhu Lata, Srikrishna Subramanian, TNC Ramya
pmc-13594953.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microbial carbohydrate-active enzymes often contain non-catalytic carbohydrate-binding modules, which enhance the activity of the catalytic domain by proximity, targeting, or disruptive effects. We have previously biochemically characterized a GH29 α-L-fucosidase from Streptosporangium roseum, demonstrated that its C-terminal F-type lectin domain (FLD) improves the enzyme activity of its tandem N-terminal α-L-fucosidase domain towards fucooligosaccharides, and proposed a “bind and jump” model to explain this FLD-driven improvement of α-L-fucosidase activity.

pmc-13678518.title: Experimental manipulation of ecological constraints influences conflict but not cooperation in the humbug damselfish Dascyllus aruanus
pmc-13678518.creator: Rebecca Branconi, Marian Y L Wong, Daniel B Stouffer, Theresa Rueger, Peter Buston
pmc-13678518.description: Animal societies vary widely in levels of cooperation and conflict, and understanding the causes of this variation is a central goal in evolutionary biology. As with other features of animal societies, relatedness, competitiveness and ecological constraints (e.g. habitat saturation and risks of dispersal) have been proposed as key factors explaining variation in cooperation and conflict.
